title: Oxford Economics launches AskOE AI Model Assistant, the world’s first AI assistant for macro modelling
gist: Product announcement: Oxford Economics launched AskOE AI Model Assistant, a conversational interface that converts natural-language assumptions into inputs for its Global Economic Model and benchmarks scenario results against its baseline. It extends OE's AI suite (Business Foresight, Executive Lens, MCP integrations) aimed at embedding its research and models in client planning workflows.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics has launched AskOE AI Model Assistant, billed as the world's first AI assistant for macro modelling, letting users build and run macroeconomic scenarios through natural language.
insights.speaker: Madeleine Henry
insights.so_what: Lowers the skill barrier for running structural macro scenarios; non-modellers at corporates and investors can stress-test plans without economist intermediaries.
insights.quote: enabling users to build and run macroeconomic scenarios through natural language
insights.locator: Oxford Economics has launched AskOEAI Model

insights.claim: The Model Assistant translates user assumptions into inputs for Oxford Economics' flagship Global Economic Model (GEM), uses OE research to shape scenarios, runs them through the model, and benchmarks results against OE's latest baseline.
insights.speaker: Madeleine Henry
insights.so_what: Outputs remain anchored to a proprietary structural model and house baseline, so LLM is an interface layer rather than the forecaster - results inherit GEM's assumptions and biases.
insights.quote: translates users’ assumptions into the appropriate inputs for its flagship Global Economic Model (GEM)
insights.locator: Purpose-built by Oxford Economics’ modelling and AI

insights.claim: Oxford Economics argues the key bottleneck in scenario analysis under high uncertainty is converting 'what if' questions into modellable, benchmarkable scenarios quickly - which conversational AI is meant to solve.
insights.speaker: Madeleine Henry
insights.so_what: Demand for rapid shock analysis rises in high-uncertainty regimes; tools compressing scenario turnaround could become standard in corporate planning and risk functions.
insights.quote: The challenge is turning those questions into scenarios that can be modelled and benchmarked quickly and easily.

insights.claim: Model Assistant is part of a broader Oxford Economics AI suite including AskOE Business Foresight, Executive Lens, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations that plug OE research and data into clients' existing AI tools.
insights.speaker: Madeleine Henry
insights.so_what: Macro research vendors are repositioning as data/model providers into client AI stacks via MCP, signalling distribution shifting from reports to agent-accessible feeds.
insights.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations that connect Oxford Economics’ research and data with the AI tools clients already use
insights.locator: Model Assistant builds on Oxford Economics’ wider

insights.claim: Oxford Economics frames its AI investment as a way to help clients extract more value from its economic expertise, whether building business forecasts, running scenarios, or using OE intelligence inside their own AI tools.
insights.speaker: Madeleine Henry
insights.so_what: AI is treated as a monetisation and retention lever for proprietary research and models rather than a replacement for economists.
insights.quote: Our investment in AI is about helping clients unlock more value from our economic expertise.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics states it covers over 200 countries, 100 industrial sectors and 8,000 cities and regions, which underpins the breadth of data its AI tools draw on.
insights.speaker: Madeleine Henry
insights.so_what: Breadth of proprietary coverage is the moat that differentiates vendor AI assistants from generic LLMs answering macro questions.
insights.quote: Covering over 200 countries, 100 industrial sectors and 8,000 cities and regions
